ENGLISH LANGUAGE — TERMLY EXAM #15 (TERM 3)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What does 'rinse' mean? (1 mark)
   A. To make dirty
   B. To dry with cloth
   C. To wash with clean water to take off soap
   D. To cook

2. Which conjunction means the same as 'but' in 'The room was small, ____ it was very clean'? (1 mark)
   A. yet
   B. so
   C. nor
   D. for

3. What does a referee do? (1 mark)
   A. Trains the team
   B. Sells tickets
   C. Cleans the field
   D. Controls a game and makes sure the rules are followed

4. Which sentence has the /ð/ sound in the first word? (1 mark)
   A. Three players scored.
   B. The team practised hard.
   C. Think before you act.
   D. Thank the coach.

5. Which is a safe habit when searching online? (1 mark)
   A. Telling strangers your password
   B. Sharing your address
   C. Clicking every pop-up
   D. Using sites your teacher approves

6. What is at the centre of a mind map? (1 mark)
   A. The date
   B. The last idea
   C. The author's name
   D. The main topic

7. Which word completes 'The coach is asking, "____ scored the goal?"'? (1 mark)
   A. Where
   B. When
   C. Whose
   D. Who

8. After 'does' or 'did', which form of the main verb do we use? (1 mark)
   A. The -ing form
   B. The past participle
   C. The base form
   D. The plural form

9. Which is the correct spelling of the word for a person who is not just an acquaintance? (1 mark)
   A. friend
   B. freind
   C. frind
   D. frend

10. Which of these is a homophone pair? (1 mark)
   A. their and there
   B. run and walk
   C. big and large
   D. hot and cold

11. Which word has the long vowel /ɔː/? (1 mark)
   A. cup
   B. mud
   C. door
   D. bus

12. Which answer suits 'Do you sweep every day?' (1 mark)
   A. It is mine.
   B. At six o'clock.
   C. In the compound.
   D. Yes, I do.

13. In 'The Clean-Up Day', which proverb did Kamau use about fixing the hole in the fence? (1 mark)
   A. A stitch in time saves nine
   B. Prevention is better than cure
   C. Look before you leap
   D. Many hands make light work

14. Which time word often goes with the present perfect? (1 mark)
   A. in 2010
   B. yesterday
   C. last week
   D. already

15. What is the past participle of 'go'? (1 mark)
   A. went
   B. goed
   C. gone
   D. going

16. Which is a sentence in the future tense about tomorrow? (1 mark)
   A. I was visiting her.
   B. Tomorrow I will visit my grandmother.
   C. I visit my grandmother now.
   D. Yesterday I visited my grandmother.

17. Which word can help you show the order of events in a diary? (1 mark)
   A. then
   B. desk
   C. broom
   D. green

18. Which word has a silent t? (1 mark)
   A. tent
   B. listen
   C. ten
   D. table

19. What does 'profit' mean? (1 mark)
   A. A tax
   B. A gift
   C. Money gained when you sell for more than you paid
   D. Money lost in a sale

20. Which preposition completes: 'The bank is ____ the school and the post office.'? (1 mark)
   A. between
   B. into
   C. among
   D. through

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Rewrite in the past tense: 'Today we sweep the compound and plant a tree.' (2 marks)

22. Write four sentences about cleaning your classroom that use and, but, so and or. (4 marks)

23. Write three yes/no questions about keeping the compound clean. (3 marks)

24. Rewrite using the past perfect: 'The bus left. Then I arrived.' (2 marks)

25. Explain the meaning of 'tax' and 'fine'. (3 marks)

26. Write four sentences for a short speech about your favourite game. (4 marks)

27. Explain the difference between 'in' and 'into'. Give one sentence for each. (3 marks)

28. Explain the difference between 'but' and 'so' with an example of each. (4 marks)

29. Give directions from your classroom to the school gate using at least three prepositions. (3 marks)

30. Make two sentences with 'very ... but ...' about shopping. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — TERMLY EXAM #15 (TERM 3) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — To wash with clean water to take off soap
   You rinse after using soap.

2. A — yet
   'Yet' shows a surprise, like 'but'.

3. D — Controls a game and makes sure the rules are followed
   A referee is the official in charge.

4. B — The team practised hard.
   'The' has voiced 'th'; 'think', 'three' and 'thank' have unvoiced 'th'.

5. D — Using sites your teacher approves
   Approved sites and private details keep you safe.

6. D — The main topic
   The main topic is in the middle.

7. D — Who
   'Who' asks about a person.

8. C — The base form
   For example: 'When does she practise?'

9. A — friend
   Friend is spelt f-r-i-e-n-d.

10. A — their and there
   They sound the same but are spelt differently.

11. C — door
   'Door' has /ɔː/; the others have the short /ʌ/.

12. D — Yes, I do.
   A yes/no question needs a yes or no answer.

13. A — A stitch in time saves nine
   He wanted to fix the small hole before it got worse.

14. D — already
   'Already' fits the present perfect; finished-time words do not.

15. C — gone
   Go, went, gone.

16. B — Tomorrow I will visit my grandmother.
   'Will visit' shows the future.

17. A — then
   'Then' is a time word.

18. B — listen
   'Listen' is said 'lisen'.

19. C — Money gained when you sell for more than you paid
   Profit is the gain from selling.

20. A — between
   'Between' is used for two things.

SECTION B
----
21. (2 marks)
   Answer: Today we swept the compound and planted a tree.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for swept and 1 for planted.

22. (4 marks)
   Answer: Any four correct sentences, each with the named conjunction.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct sentence.

23. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example: Do you sweep the compound? Is the bin covered? Can we plant a tree?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct question.

24. (2 marks)
   Answer: The bus had left before I arrived. (Or: When I arrived, the bus had left.)
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 'had left' and 1 for the linking word.

25. (3 marks)
   Answer: Tax is money paid to the government to help run the country. A fine is money paid as a punishment for breaking a rule or law.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 for showing a difference.

26. (4 marks)
   Answer: A greeting, the name of the game, a reason, and a closing.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part.

27. (3 marks)
   Answer: 'In' shows where something is: The coins are in the box. 'Into' shows movement to the inside: She put the coins into the box.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 for examples.

28. (4 marks)
   Answer: 'But' shows a difference: It was late, but we stayed. 'So' shows a result: It was late, so we left.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 mark for each example.

29. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example: Go out of the classroom, walk along the corridor and go past the office to the gate.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct preposition.

30. (2 marks)
   Answer: For example: The mango is very sweet, but it is small. The bag is very nice, but it is expensive.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct sentence.
